# defectdojo_sla_configuration (Resource)

Manages a DefectDojo SLA configuration: the number of days in which findings of each severity must be remediated. Products use it through `sla_configuration_id`.

DefectDojo refuses to delete an SLA configuration that products use: move them to another one first. The `Default` SLA configuration (ID 1), which DefectDojo creates and gives products that don't name another, can't be deleted: import it to manage its days, and destroying it only removes it from the Terraform state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "defectdojo_sla_configuration" "strict" {
  name        = "Internet-facing"
  description = "Shorter SLAs for internet-facing products"
  critical    = 3
  high        = 14
  medium      = 60
  low         = 90
  enforce_low = false
}

resource "defectdojo_product" "storefront" {
  name                 = "Storefront"
  description          = "The online shop"
  product_type_id      = 1
  sla_configuration_id = defectdojo_sla_configuration.strict.id
}

# DefectDojo's Default SLA configuration, which products get unless they
# name another, can be imported and managed, but not deleted. Changing its
# days makes DefectDojo recalculate the SLA dates of every product that uses
# it, and locks them until that has finished.
import {
  to = defectdojo_sla_configuration.default
  id = "1"
}

resource "defectdojo_sla_configuration" "default" {
  name        = "Default"
  description = "The Default SLA Configuration. Products not using an explicit SLA Configuration will use this one."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the SLA configuration, at most 128 characters, without leading or trailing whitespace, which DefectDojo removes. Names are unique, compared case-sensitively.

### Optional

- `critical` (Number) The number of days in which critical findings must be remediated, at least 1. Defaults to `7`. A change makes DefectDojo recalculate the SLA expiration dates of the findings of the products that use the configuration, which its Celery workers do in the background; until that has finished, DefectDojo refuses another change of the days or `enforce_*` attributes of the configuration, and of the SLA configuration of those products. With the system setting `enable_finding_sla` off, DefectDojo never finishes, so the days can then change only once.
- `description` (String) The description of the SLA configuration, at most 512 characters, without leading or trailing whitespace, which DefectDojo removes.
- `enforce_critical` (Boolean) Whether critical findings get an SLA expiration date. Defaults to `true`. A change makes DefectDojo recalculate the SLA expiration dates of the findings of the products that use the configuration, which its Celery workers do in the background; until that has finished, DefectDojo refuses another change of the days or `enforce_*` attributes of the configuration, and of the SLA configuration of those products. With the system setting `enable_finding_sla` off, DefectDojo never finishes, so the days can then change only once.
- `enforce_high` (Boolean) Whether high findings get an SLA expiration date. Defaults to `true`. A change makes DefectDojo recalculate the SLA expiration dates of the findings of the products that use the configuration, which its Celery workers do in the background; until that has finished, DefectDojo refuses another change of the days or `enforce_*` attributes of the configuration, and of the SLA configuration of those products. With the system setting `enable_finding_sla` off, DefectDojo never finishes, so the days can then change only once.
- `enforce_low` (Boolean) Whether low findings get an SLA expiration date. Defaults to `true`. A change makes DefectDojo recalculate the SLA expiration dates of the findings of the products that use the configuration, which its Celery workers do in the background; until that has finished, DefectDojo refuses another change of the days or `enforce_*` attributes of the configuration, and of the SLA configuration of those products. With the system setting `enable_finding_sla` off, DefectDojo never finishes, so the days can then change only once.
- `enforce_medium` (Boolean) Whether medium findings get an SLA expiration date. Defaults to `true`. A change makes DefectDojo recalculate the SLA expiration dates of the findings of the products that use the configuration, which its Celery workers do in the background; until that has finished, DefectDojo refuses another change of the days or `enforce_*` attributes of the configuration, and of the SLA configuration of those products. With the system setting `enable_finding_sla` off, DefectDojo never finishes, so the days can then change only once.
- `high` (Number) The number of days in which high findings must be remediated, at least 1. Defaults to `30`. A change makes DefectDojo recalculate the SLA expiration dates of the findings of the products that use the configuration, which its Celery workers do in the background; until that has finished, DefectDojo refuses another change of the days or `enforce_*` attributes of the configuration, and of the SLA configuration of those products. With the system setting `enable_finding_sla` off, DefectDojo never finishes, so the days can then change only once.
- `low` (Number) The number of days in which low findings must be remediated, at least 1. Defaults to `120`. A change makes DefectDojo recalculate the SLA expiration dates of the findings of the products that use the configuration, which its Celery workers do in the background; until that has finished, DefectDojo refuses another change of the days or `enforce_*` attributes of the configuration, and of the SLA configuration of those products. With the system setting `enable_finding_sla` off, DefectDojo never finishes, so the days can then change only once.
- `medium` (Number) The number of days in which medium findings must be remediated, at least 1. Defaults to `90`. A change makes DefectDojo recalculate the SLA expiration dates of the findings of the products that use the configuration, which its Celery workers do in the background; until that has finished, DefectDojo refuses another change of the days or `enforce_*` attributes of the configuration, and of the SLA configuration of those products. With the system setting `enable_finding_sla` off, DefectDojo never finishes, so the days can then change only once.
- `restart_sla_on_reactivation` (Boolean) Whether findings that a reimport reactivates get a new SLA period. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The ID of the SLA configuration.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = defectdojo_sla_configuration.example
  identity = {
    id = 3
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (Number) ID of the SLA configuration

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# SLA configurations are imported by their numeric ID
terraform import defectdojo_sla_configuration.example <id>
```
